The best-supported answer from my own count is 29, which none of the three solutions gives. Solution 1 is the closest in method.

**Reading the diagram.**
- Top view (S): `+++++`, `+----`, `+++++`, `----+`, `+++++`.
- Front view (M): `+++++`, then four rows of `+-+-+`.
- Right view (T): `+++++`, then four rows of `--+--`.

A unit cube can be red only if all three lines of sight through it show `+`. Since we want the maximum, every allowed cell is made red. Each `+` is then covered as long as at least one cell on its line of sight is allowed.

**Counting allowed cells.**
- **Top layer.** The front and right views are fully `+` in the top row, so only the top view limits it. That gives 5 + 1 + 5 + 1 + 5 = 17 cells.
- **Each of the four lower layers.** The right view allows only the middle depth. The top view row at middle depth is `+++++`, so it allows every column. The front view allows columns 1, 3 and 5. That gives 3 cells per layer, or 12 in total.

The total is 17 + 12 = 29. Every `+` is covered: the top layer handles the top view and the top rows of the other views, and the lower-layer cells handle the stems of the M and the T.

**Checking the solutions.**
- **Solution 1:** Its method is correct, but it misread the right view's bottom row as `+-+-+`, which should be `--+--`. This adds 6 spurious cells (9 instead of 3 in the bottom layer) and gives 35 instead of 29.
- **Solution 2:** Its enumeration of allowed cells is inconsistent and does not match the views, so 27 is wrong.
- **Solution 3:** It ignores the top layer's many allowed cells and counts only part of the allowed set, so 20 is wrong.

Solution 1 has the correct approach with a single misreading, so it is the best choice.

CHOICE: 1
